answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a vertex as the anchor of the cost.
